name: Persian Blue
lede: Persian blue is a name two dictionaries use for two different things: a strong blue, and an old trade name for Prussian blue.

sections.title: One name, two meanings
sections.body:
Paterson defines Persian blue as a strong blue and, in a second sense, a pale violet [1]. The Pigment Compendium instead lists it among the many names for [[prussian-blue]], beside Paris blue, Saxon blue and Haarlem blue [2].

Books disagree, then, on whether it is a hue or a pigment. The Compendium adds a warning that applies to the whole list: place names do not necessarily imply a place of origin, and it chooses Persian blue as its example [2]. Neither book ties the name to Persia itself [1][2].

sections.title: The swatch
sections.body: The swatch is the library value for the name, a strong saturated blue [3]. Paterson files Persian blue in its blue group, next to Paris blue, Prussian blue and Sevres blue [1]. Screen colors are approximate [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The books say little more. Five passages mention the name in the concordance, three of them index lists in Paterson and two in the Compendium [1][2]. Treat it as a historical label more than a stable color.

origin.named_after: origin undocumented; the Compendium warns place names need not mark a place of origin

disambiguation.gloss: the pigment the Compendium says this name was also used for

questions.q: What does the Pigment Compendium say place names such as Persian blue do not necessarily imply?
Paterson gives Persian blue two senses: a strong blue and a pale violet.

openers: Persian blue is, in one dictionary, just another name for Prussian blue.

issues: Books disagree: hue vs Prussian blue synonym
